Class 3 · Chapter 4 of 10

Shapes, reflections and boundaries

Describe flat and solid shapes, find symmetry and measure the boundary.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Equal parts and fractions. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can describe flat and solid shapes.
  • I can find symmetry and mirror images.
  • I can find a shape's boundary length.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Describe a flat shape

Say how many sides and corners a flat shape has.

A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners. Opposite sides are the same length.

Screen 2 of 5

Describe a solid

A cube has 6 flat faces. A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved surface.

A cone has 1 flat face, 1 curved surface and a tip. A sphere has no flat face.

Screen 3 of 5

Lines of symmetry

If you fold on a line of symmetry, both halves match.

Here the line goes down the middle. Each shaded square has a twin.

Screen 4 of 5

Mirror images

A mirror image is flipped, not turned.

Left becomes right. The top stays on top when the mirror is a standing line.

Screen 5 of 5

Walk round the boundary

The perimeter is the length all the way round a shape.

This rectangle is 3 squares long and 2 wide. Count the edges: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10.

Words to know
symmetry
Both sides of a line match exactly.
perimeter
The distance all the way round the edge of a shape.
face
A flat surface of a solid.

For parents

What your child learns

A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves. A rectangle has 2 such lines. Solids can be named by faces and corners, and cubes in a stack can be counted by layers.

A common slip

Children often count the diagonals of a rectangle as lines of symmetry. Fold a paper copy to test. If the halves do not match, it is not a line.

5-minute home activity: Fold to test

  1. Cut a rectangle and a square from paper.
  2. Fold each one so the halves match.
  3. Count each different fold that works.
  4. Stack small blocks in layers and count the ones above the base.
